title: Casework | TigerGraph fraud investigation
text: This is Casework, a fraud investigation prototype for the TigerGraph Hacker House Goa challenge. This edited walkthrough uses actual screens captured from the running application. The system combines a TigerGraph evidence graph, native vector retrieval, the official MCP server, and a local language model. All customer replies are explicitly simulated. No card operation or regulatory filing is sent.

title: 1. Start with an uncertain trigger
text: We begin with case H H G zero ten. The transaction amount is one thousand dollars and three cents. Its risk score triggered investigation, but is not treated as proof. The agent retrieves customer history, explicitly known card transactions, device neighbors, and past cases. Before verification, it recommends asking the customer, creating an internal case, and escalating the uncertainty because exposure exceeds five hundred dollars.

title: 2. Request controlled evidence
text: The analyst selects an explicit simulated customer denial and starts the investigation through the interface. The running status reflects a real server job. The agent calls TigerGraph through MCP, plans a semantic retrieval query, reads historical and policy context, and reviews the evidence. The assumption is recorded in the case. It is never presented as a reply actually received from a customer.

title: 3. Update recommendations and approvals
text: When the simulated denial arrives, the recommendation changes. Under rule R two, the agent recommends blocking the affected card and retaining the internal case. The block requires level one approval at this exposure. Because the amount exceeds one thousand dollars, a suspicious activity report is also recommended, with level two approval. The before and after recommendations remain visible together, so the change can be audited.

title: 4. Explain evidence and uncertainty
text: Each evidence item identifies its source and reference. The graph view contains relationships returned by TigerGraph, not a decorative network. Historical case narratives and policy passages provide retrieval context for the language model. Important limits remain explicit: customer history is not automatically card history, generic device profiles do not uniquely identify people, and merchant identity and settlement status are unavailable. The agent does not invent these missing facts.

title: 5. Produce a policy-controlled SAR draft
text: The report is a draft awaiting human approval. Its narrative records who, what, when, where, and why the activity is suspicious, along with the exposure and simulation assumption. A case and a regulatory report are separate outputs. Most uncertain cases do not automatically need a report. The final JSON records the recommendation and approval route; it does not claim that a real regulator received a filing.

title: 6. Preserve and reuse case memory
text: The current case is saved to TigerGraph and its payload is read back. Versioned investigation records preserve progression when a case is rerun. Later investigations retrieve earlier generated records through native vector search, with time filtering and exclusion of the current case. Generated outcomes remain labeled as simulated or unverified, separate from the supplied confirmed historical labels. The interface exposes preserved revisions and the model's uncertainty review.

title: 7. Investigate beyond the flagged transaction
text: The analyst-request case demonstrates a coordinated pattern across customers. Several transactions share a profile marked new and anonymous proxy attributes within forty eight hours. The agent records the motif as suspected undocumented abuse, includes its supporting transactions, and escalates for analyst and report review. This prototype uses heuristic probabilities, not a measured accuracy claim. The repository includes the twenty answer files, tests, technical write-up, and verification reports.
